parts.t: Neighbourhood guide · City of Surrey · Fleetwood

Fleetwood Tynehead is the MLS® area for Fleetwood in Surrey. On the MLS® map it runs roughly from 152 Street east to 176 Street (Highway 15), and from about 96 Avenue south to a line running from about 76 Avenue at 152 Street to Fraser Highway at 176 Street. The edges are approximate. The City’s Fleetwood Plan covers the land along Fraser Highway from Green Timbers Urban Forest east towards the Agricultural Land Reserve, where three SkyTrain stations are being built. Tynehead Regional Park is to the north.

Written by Jared Gibbons, REALTOR®, Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, on October 13, 2026. I have worked in Fraser Valley real estate for 11+ years. Facts come from the official sources noted on this page. Rules and boundaries change, so confirm anything important with the City of Surrey and Surrey Schools.
Not legal, planning or financial advice. Confirm zoning, plan designations and school catchments before you buy or sell.

parts.t: Fleetwood Tynehead is a highly desirable and rapidly growing community in

, known for its family-friendly neighbourhoods, excellent schools, and convenient access to parks and amenities. The area offers a wide range of real estate options, including spacious detached homes, modern townhouses, and well-located condos, making it a popular choice for families, first-time buyers, and investors.

One of the biggest draws to Fleetwood Tynehead is its central location and future SkyTrain expansion, which is expected to further increase accessibility and long-term property value. Residents enjoy close proximity to Fleetwood Park, Tynehead Regional Park, recreation centres, shopping, and major commuter routes.

With a strong sense of community, continued development, and a variety of housing styles, Fleetwood Tynehead continues to attract buyers looking for space, convenience, and solid investment potential in the Surrey real estate market.

parts.t: Plans are changing around the new SkyTrain stations. Zoning and plan designations can be different for each lot.
Council first endorsed the Fleetwood Stage 1 Plan on March 7, 2022, and an updated Stage 1 Plan on October 16, 2023.
On December 2, 2024, Council raised the Urban Residential density in the plan to a maximum of 55 units per hectare.
The plan has since been changed to match the Province’s Transit Oriented Areas law, and the City says Council will consider the updated plan in 2026.

The City’s heritage register lists two Fleetwood sites: Fleetwood Memorial United Church at 8590 160 Street, built in 1953 and now the Surrey Chinese Baptist Church, and Michael Morrisey House at 9207 160 Street.
